newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey-PENGUINS ROLL OVER DUCKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-PENGUINS ROLL OVER DUCKS.

text.p: Mario Lemieux and Petr Nedved each had two goals and an assist to help the surging Pittburgh Penguins extend their unbeaten streak to nine games with a 7-3 victory over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim on Wednesday.
Alex Hicks, Joe Dziedzic and Kevin Hatcher also scored for the Penguins, who are 7-0-2 in their last nine games.
Penguins right wing Jaromir Jagr had two assists to extend his points streak to 12 games, but had his nine-game goal-scoring streak end.
In Dallas, Joe Nieuwendyk's goal with 7:31 left in the game offset Al MacInnis' natural hat trick and lifted the Dallas Stars to a 5-5 tie with the St. Louis Blues.

St. Louis led 3-0 on MacInnis' second career hat trick before the game was 14 minutes old. But Dallas erased deficits of 4-0 and 5-4 before Nieuwendyk picked up the loose puck from along the right boards, and with Pierre Turgeon draped on his back, forehanded the puck past Grant Fuhr for his fifth goal.
"We showed an awful lot of character coming back tonight. I'm very proud of the way our club played," said Stars coach Ken Hitchcock.

In Hartford, Keith Primeau ignited a five-goal third period with a pair of goals as the Hartford Whalers extended their unbeaten streak to six games with a come-from-behind 5-2 victory over the Florida Panthers in a battle of division leaders.
Second-period gols by Bill Lindsay and Dave Lowry gave the Panthers a 2-0 lead entering the third, but the Whalers scored three goals, the first two by Primeuau, in the first 6:32.

Primeau's first goal of the game and ninth of the season 34 seconds into the third cut the deficit in half. Then Primeau flipped a backhander into the net for a 2-2 tie, and just 50 seconds later, Gerald Diduck scored on a slap shot to give the Whalers the lead for good.
In Montreal, Dixon Ward scored 2:42 into overtime to lift the Buffalo Sabres to a 3-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens.

"I can't put my finger on it, it seems that this team plays better when they are down," Ward said. "Inexperience is still showing on our team. When we get a lead, we blow it. We have not developed that killer instinct."
Domink Hasek made 43 saves, including three in overtime, for the Sabres.
In New York, Rookie defenceman Bryan Berard had a goal and an assist in a four-goal second period and Zigmund Palffy scored twice as the New York Islanders beat the New York Rangers 5-3.
The Rangers, who saw their season-high seven game unbeaten streak end, fell to 1-8-4 against the Atlantic Division this season.
"Until we start winning hockey games in our division that is going to be the focus on this team," Wayne Gretzky said.
In Vancouver, Patrick Roy made 20 saves and Peter Forsberg had three assists as the Colorado Avalanche continued their dominance over the Vancouver Canucks with a 6-1 victory.
Forsberg's three assists give him a league-leading 30 assists and 42 points.

In San Jose, Chris Terreri made 20 saves and Vlastimil Kroupa, Shean Donovan and Tony Granato scored one goal apiece as the San Jose Sharks handed the Washington Capitals their fourth consecutive loss, 3-2.
Terreri stopped five shots in the first, nine in the second and eight over the final 20 minutes to earn his fourth win.
Granato gave the Sharks a 3-1 lead 83 seconds into the third with a shorthanded marker. The Sharks lead the NHL with seven shorthanded goals.
